title: The Wrong Classroom

pre.en: Why was Chen marked absent on his first day?
pre.zh: 小陈上学第一天为什么被记了缺勤？
options: He was reading Harry Potter in class.
He was in the right room but the wrong building.

intro: 一篇新概念式的小故事：小陈给室友讲自己上中学第一天的糗事。读的时候留意过去完成时 had done：故事讲的是 2008 年那天，凡是「在那之前就已经发生」的事——前一晚研究地图、爸爸送的书、小学老师的教导——都要往回退一步。结尾有个回马枪。

sentences.en: So, Tom's got hooked on Chinese films lately, and I tend to leave my laptop lying around.
sentences.zh: Tom 最近迷上了中国电影，而我又总爱把笔记本电脑随手一放。

sentences.en: On Sunday he was looking for something to watch and found an old school photo instead.
sentences.zh: 星期天他在我电脑上找片子看，结果翻出了一张上学时的老照片。

sentences.en: There's a small boy at the back who looks completely lost.
sentences.zh: 后排有个小男孩，一脸茫然。

sentences.en: "That must be you, Chen," he said.
sentences.zh: 「这个肯定是你吧，小陈，」他说。

sentences.en: He was right.
sentences.zh: 还真让他说中了。

sentences.en: It was September 2008, my first day at secondary school.
sentences.zh: 那是 2008 年 9 月，我上中学的第一天。

sentences.en: I'd studied the school map the night before, and I'd got up at six.
sentences.zh: 前一天晚上我就把学校地图研究了一遍，早上六点就起来了。

sentences.en: I hadn't slept much, but not because I was nervous.
sentences.zh: 我没怎么睡，倒不是因为紧张。

sentences.en: Dad had given me a Harry Potter book, and I couldn't put it down.
sentences.zh: 是爸爸给了我一本《哈利·波特》，我一拿起来就放不下。

sentences.en: I'd also made room in my bag for a dictionary the size of a brick.
sentences.zh: 我还在书包里腾出地方，塞了一本砖头那么厚的词典。

sentences.en: It had cost Mum ninety-eight yuan, and she kept saying it was worth the money.
sentences.zh: 那本词典花了妈妈九十八块钱，她一个劲儿地说买得值。

sentences.en: At ten to eight, I walked confidently into Room 304 and sat at the back.
sentences.zh: 七点五十，我信心满满地走进 304 教室，在最后一排坐下。

sentences.en: The first lesson was physics, and for forty minutes I tried to take in every word.
sentences.zh: 第一节是物理课，整整四十分钟，我拼命想把每个字都听进去。

sentences.en: I'd never been into science, so I just decided secondary school was much harder.
sentences.zh: 我本来就对理科没兴趣，所以干脆认定中学就是难得多。

sentences.en: I felt a bit out of place, but I told myself it was no big deal.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己有点格格不入，但我跟自己说，没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: At first nobody noticed me.
sentences.zh: 一开始谁也没注意到我。

sentences.en: I found out later that the other students had assumed I was someone's little brother.
sentences.zh: 后来我才知道，班上同学都以为我是谁家的弟弟。

sentences.en: Then the teacher asked a question about speed.
sentences.zh: 后来老师问了一个关于速度的问题。

sentences.en: My primary school teachers had always said, "If you know the answer, put your hand up."
sentences.zh: 小学老师一直跟我们说：「知道答案就举手。」

sentences.en: So I put my hand up.
sentences.zh: 于是我就举了手。

sentences.en: The teacher looked at me and said, "And who are you?"
sentences.zh: 老师看了我一眼，说：「你是哪位？」

sentences.en: That was when I realised I'd got the building wrong.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，我才反应过来自己走错了楼。

sentences.en: My class was in Room 304 of Building B, where I'd already been marked absent on the register.
sentences.zh: 我的班在 B 栋的 304，那边的点名册上已经把我记成缺课了。

sentences.en: Anyway, that afternoon I made friends with Liu Yang, who thought it was the coolest thing ever.
sentences.zh: 反正那天下午，我和刘洋交上了朋友，他觉得这事简直酷毙了。

sentences.en: Three years later, the same physics teacher handed back my final exam.
sentences.zh: 三年后，还是那位物理老师把我的毕业考试卷发了回来。

sentences.en: "You again," he said.
sentences.zh: 「又是你，」他说。

sentences.en: "At least you're in the right room this time."
sentences.zh: 「好歹这回没走错教室。」

cards.note: to start to enjoy something so much that you want to do it all the time
to leave things in places where they should not be, instead of putting them away
英国 11 到 16、18 岁上的学校；小学是 primary school。
to find something so interesting that you cannot stop reading, watching or using it
to move or remove things so that there is space for something else
cards.tip: room 在这里是「空间」，不可数，不加 a；在哪儿腾地方可以插在中间：make room in the car for …
cards.example: We moved the sofa to make room for a bigger table.

cards.note: the size of a brick 形容又厚又重，和中文「砖头那么厚」正好一样。
to be good enough to justify the price you pay
cards.tip: worth 后面直接跟名词，不加 of；更强的说法是 be worth every penny。
cards.example: The tickets were expensive, but the show was worth the money.

cards.note: 形容词 confident；名词 confidence。
虽然以 s 结尾，却是不可数名词，动词用单数：Physics is hard.

cards.zh: 理解并记住（听到、读到的东西）
cards.note: to understand and remember something that you hear or read
cards.tip: 宾语是代词时必须放中间：take it in；名词可以放后面：take in every word。
cards.example: There was so much information on my first day that I couldn't take it all in.

cards.note: to be very interested in an activity or subject and enjoy it
cards.tip: 口语说法；I'm not really into … 比 I don't like … 委婉。后面接名词或 doing。
cards.example: My sister is really into rock climbing at the moment.

cards.zh: 觉得格格不入；觉得自己不该在这儿
cards.note: to feel uncomfortable because you are different from the people around you
cards.tip: 可以加 a bit、completely 调程度；东西放得不合适说 look out of place。
cards.example: I felt out of place at the party because everyone else knew each other.

cards.note: used to say that something is not important or not a problem
at the beginning, before something changes
cards.tip: 后面通常跟着转折（but、then、later）；first of all 是列举时的「首先」，别混。
cards.example: At first I hated the new office, but now I quite like it.

cards.note: 没有证据就这么认为，常常是错的；名词 assumption。
to raise your arm in a class or meeting because you want to answer or ask something
cards.tip: your 要跟着人称变：put my hand up、put their hands up；也可以说 raise your hand。Hands up! 是「举手」的口令。
cards.example: If you have a question, just put your hand up.

cards.note: to make a mistake about something, for example a time, a place or a fact
cards.tip: sth 放在 get 和 wrong 中间：get the time wrong；全弄错了说 get it all wrong。英式英语的过去分词是 got。
cards.example: Sorry, I got the date wrong — the party is next Friday.

cards.note: mark sb absent 记某人缺勤；反义词是 present（出席的）。
英国学校每天早上点名叫 take the register；动词 register 是「登记、注册」。
to start a friendship with someone
cards.tip: friends 一定用复数，哪怕只交了一个朋友：make friends with Tom，不说 make a friend with Tom。
cards.example: My son made friends with the boy next door in his first week.
